references_named: Ewald Hering, opponent-process theory of colour vision
rationale: The work earns a strong novelty of location: the artwork literally does not exist on screen at the moment of its completion — it is rendered by the viewer's own retina after the timed withdrawal. Concept and execution collapse cleanly (P1): the 20s timed fade, fixation dot and depleting ring are the physiological instrument, not decoration. Johns is a fresh patron saint for the catalogue and slots into the Pop/appropriation lineage beside Pop Whaam! and the Warhol hamburger. The caption's dry inversion of the house line 'the pixels are the message' is the cheerful-cynic voice landing precisely.
reservations: The afterimage depends on viewer physiology, ambient light and display quality — the work will fail partially in bright rooms, on washed-out laptop screens, or for inattentive viewers, which slightly undercuts the universality claim implicit in P3. The underlying optical phenomenon is centuries old; the novelty must rest entirely on the timed web surface and the Johns framing, which it does, but the effect itself is not new to human experience.
revision_suggestion: Consider a subtle honesty signal in the caption — e.g., a one-line 'best in a dim room' note already in the intro, or a tiny 'if the flag didn't appear, your screen is too bright' line — that turns the contingency into part of the conceptual frame rather than a hidden failure mode. Optionally, log a brief localStorage-free fixation-stability probe to deepen P1's claim that the mechanism is doing real physiological work.
